headline_marked: 2 [[Indian nationals shot by BSF]] after being mistaken for Bangladeshis
headline: 2 Indian nationals shot by BSF after being mistaken for Bangladeshis
summary: The victims, residents of Assam, were beaten and shot by the BSF inside Indian territory before being left at the Bangladesh border.
details: Two Indian citizens from the South Salmara Mancachar district of Assam were shot by the Border Security Force (BSF) on Sunday night at the Ulipur border in Kurigram.
The victims, Ismail Hossain and Abdul Alim, were allegedly beaten and shot after BSF members suspected them of being Bangladeshi cattle smugglers.
Ismail Hossain reported that he was simply trying to tie up his buffaloes when he was detained, beaten with sticks, and shot by the BSF before being left at the zero line of the Bangladesh border.
The injured men were rescued by local Bangladeshi boatmen and citizens, who first took them to the Ulipur Upazila Health Complex and later to Rangpur Medical College (RpMC) Hospital.

Surgeons at RpMC have successfully performed operations to remove bullet splinters. However, one of the victims remains in critical condition due to multiple injuries to the abdomen and a rib fracture.
Brigadier General Ashikur Rahman, Director of RpMC Hospital, confirmed that the victims were shot within Indian territory and entered Bangladesh for medical help.
The hospital is providing all necessary medical care, including medicines and pathological tests, free of charge on humanitarian grounds.
caption:
Mistaken for foreigners, two Indian citizens were beaten and shot by their own border guards.

Two Indian citizens from the South Salmara Mancachar district of Assam were shot by the Border Security Force (BSF) on Sunday night at the Ulipur border in Kurigram.

The victims, Ismail Hossain and Abdul Alim, were allegedly beaten and shot after BSF members suspected them of being Bangladeshi cattle smugglers.

Ismail Hossain reported that he was simply trying to tie up his buffaloes when he was detained, beaten with sticks, and shot by the BSF before being left at the zero line of the Bangladesh border.

The injured men were rescued by local Bangladeshi boatmen and citizens, who first took them to the Ulipur Upazila Health Complex and later to Rangpur Medical College (RpMC) Hospital.

Surgeons at RpMC have successfully performed operations to remove bullet splinters. However, one of the victims remains in critical condition due to multiple injuries to the abdomen and a rib fracture.

Brigadier General Ashikur Rahman, Director of RpMC Hospital, confirmed that the victims were shot within Indian territory and entered Bangladesh for medical help.

The hospital is providing all necessary medical care, including medicines and pathological tests, free of charge on humanitarian grounds.

#BSF #IndiaBangladeshBorder #HumanRights #Kurigram #Assam #News

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune
